speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To begin your evaluation for dizziness, nausea, and imbalance, can you tell me if your spinning sensation is constant or does it occur only when you move your head? Also, have you noticed any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or trouble speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Vestibular Neuritis. The patient describes a constant, low-grade spinning sensation with nausea that is partially relieved by diphenhydramine, and notably lacks the positional triggers typical of benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) or the auditory symptoms associated with Meniere's disease. The recent garlic intake is likely unrelated to the vestibular pathology.
